text:
sana: anyone hitting weird redwoodctl login behavior when running under sudo? did a support session on a jumpbox and the profile ended up under /root so local serve couldn't pick it up.
ryan: ugh yes, seen that with other CLIs. quick repro?
sana: steps i used:
```
$ ssh jumpbox
$ sudo redwoodctl login
Logged in as sana@example.com
Wrote profile to /root/.redwood/profiles/default.json
```
Then on the same box as regular user: `redwoodctl local serve` -> error about missing profile.
ryan: so it's just HOME being /root when sudo runs. did you try `sudo -E` to preserve env?
sana: tried `sudo -E`, still wrote to /root. `echo $HOME` under sudo shows /root. The client doesn't have a flag i could find to specify config dir at login stage.
irene: quick workaround: set REDWOODCTL_HOME before running login, e.g. `sudo REDWOODCTL_HOME=/home/sana/.redwood redwoodctl login` — that forces it to write there.
sam: can we add a clearer warning in the CLI when HOME != real user home? like "running as root will write to /root — use --config or REDWOODCTL_HOME"
alex: agreed. also we should document the recommended flow for admins doing remote support (don't use sudo, use `--config` or a scoped token).
sana: logging this as a DX bug rn, but wanted to share the quick fix. i also tried moving the file out of /root and setting file perms, `redwoodctl local serve` still didn't pick it up until i ran `redwoodctl config set active-profile default` as the user.
ryan: can you paste the exact error `local serve` shows?
sana: output:
```
$ redwoodctl local serve
Error: no active profile found. checked /home/sana/.redwood/profiles and /root/.redwood/profiles
Use `redwoodctl login` to create a profile or `redwoodctl config set active-profile <name>` to select one.
```
dev-bot: deploy-checker: new issue created: #4123 (dx: redwoodctl sudo/home profile mismatch) :white_check_mark:
alex: for a long-term fix we should: 1) make login accept `--config`/`--home` so admins can target a path, 2) add a warning when effective UID != real UID, and 3) add a migration command like `redwoodctl profile migrate --from /root` (or at least document manual steps).
irene: i'll pick up the CLI warning patch. small change: detect if getenv("SUDO_USER") is present and print a message with suggested commands instead of silently writing to /root.
sana: thanks — that should avoid a bunch of support churn. i added repro steps + workaround to the issue. :+1:
ryan: can we also add a short FAQ blurb in the installer docs (jumpbox / remote support) so SREs don't run into this?
alex: yes I'll add a note in the devex docs and reference the issue.
sana: leaving the support notes here for anyone else who runs into it — TL;DR: avoid `sudo redwoodctl login` unless you know you want the profile in root; use `REDWOODCTL_HOME` or `--config` to target a non-root path, or run login as the actual user.
